infra.description: Read-only data-driven control panel for the WireGuard mesh + wstunnel TCP/443 fallback. Mimics Headscale's UI shape but holds zero state and exposes zero mutations — pure observability over the existing declarative VPN data (cloud-data-topology.json + bb-net_vpn/build.json + terraform.json). Snapshot is frozen at deploy time; the page hydrates from PORTAL_DATA, no runtime fetch.

infra.name: wireguard-mesh-ws-tunnel
infra.description: WireGuard-over-TCP/443 fallback for hostile networks (airport / hotel / corporate guest Wi-Fi blocking UDP). Sibling to bb-net_wireguard-mesh (the panel) — this folder owns the wstunnel-server that terminates WSS on gcp-proxy and forwards UDP to the kernel WG listener at 127.0.0.1:51820. UDP/51820 remains the primary transport; this kicks in only when clients can't reach UDP.

apps.name: openclaw
apps.description: OpenClaw (MIT, github.com/openclaw/openclaw) on oci-apps — the open-source personal agent gateway, as a fourth fleet agent next to hermes, goose and claude. Upstream's own image, unmodified. Its gateway listens on 127.0.0.1 only (host network, auth mode none, the documented trusted-loopback setup) with the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions enabled; the fleet reaches it ONLY through the agent gateway my-ai-api (X-Agent-Mode: openclaw). Its model calls go back through that same gateway's OpenRouter face, which holds the key, so this service has no secret at all. Never public, never on the mesh directly.
